Heavy Rainfall floods Tripura Districts; MP Biplab Kumar Deb calls for swift relief measures
Torrential rains over the past two days have inundated large parts of West Tripura district and adjoining regions, leaving families displaced and agricultural lands submerged. As floodwaters continue to rise, Member of Parliament and former Chief Minister Biplab Kumar Deb has urged authorities to ensure immediate rescue, relief, and administrative support for affected residents.
In a message shared on social media Sunday, Deb confirmed that he has spoken with officials to guarantee rescue operations, relief distribution, and all necessary administrative assistance in flood-hit areas. He emphasized that the administration is working actively and with urgency to deliver aid to those in distress.
Heavy rainfall has left several villages waterlogged, with homes, roads, and marketplaces submerged. Families in low-lying areas have been forced to move belongings to safer places, while many have already taken shelter in temporary camps. The rising water has disrupted normal life, and fears remain that further showers could worsen the situation.
Deb urged residents to remain cautious and maintain close communication with local authorities. He advised people to avoid venturing into risk-prone zones unless necessary and to strictly follow instructions issued by the administration. “The government is committed to standing by the flood-affected families. Relief and assistance will reach them without delay,” his statement read.
District officials have assured that rescue teams are on the ground, monitoring water levels and assisting families in relocation. Relief materials including food, drinking water, and medical supplies are being prepared for distribution. Boats have been deployed to reach waterlogged areas, and shelters are being readied for vulnerable households.
For residents of West Tripura and adjoining flood-hit zones, the disaster is not only a disruption of daily life but also a reminder of the fragility of flood-prone communities against sudden climatic events. With rainfall continuing, the coming hours will be critical in determining how far floodwaters spread and how effectively relief measures can mitigate the impact.
